text: For a source with probabilities 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/8, Huffman coding achieved exactly 1.75 bits per symbol — the entropy. Why exactly?
choices: Every probability is a power of two, so each ideal code length -log₂ pᵢ is a whole number.
Huffman coding always achieves the entropy; the theorem guarantees it for any source.
The string was short enough that rounding effects cancelled out.
The four symbols happened to form a balanced tree, which is the optimal shape.
explanation: Huffman produces integer-length code words, so it hits the entropy exactly when the ideal lengths are already integers — here 1, 2, 3, 3. Otherwise it is within one bit per symbol and no better integer-length code exists. Arithmetic coding closes the remaining gap by abandoning the whole-number requirement, which is what modern compressors use.
